Article Title: 'Mithai khilao, you are Gujarat CM now': PM Modi recalls how journalists broke the news to him
Article Text:
He said the media played an important role in keeping democracy vibrant and added that “nothing is impossible in journalism”.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday recalled how a group of journalists once informed him that he had become the chief minister of Gujarat, asking him to distribute sweets.Addressing journalists at the BJP headquarters, PM Modi said only a few senior party leaders were aware of the development when a group of journalists walked into his room and told him, “You are the CM of Gujarat now, mithai khilao. ”Recalling his journey with the media, PM Modi said he had witnessed its transformation from the days of press releases to the present era of Instagram reels. He also remembered his early days when he would arrange chairs at similar gatherings.PM Modi praised journalists for their role in keeping democracy vibrant, saying, “A vast diversity of thought sustains our democracy and keeps it vibrant—a process in which the Indian media plays a truly vital role.”Highlighting the dedication of field reporters, he said they often head towards disaster sites when others are moving away. “When a disaster strikes—be it an accident, an earthquake, or a devastating flood—while the rest of the world might flee from the scene, our field reporters head straight toward it... Such dedication is rare, and I have always held it in the highest regard,” he said.The prime minister also urged media organisations to highlight India's achievements and success stories, saying that considerable work was already being done in this regard.He called on journalists to spread awareness about the fight against drug abuse.Referring to India's ambition of becoming a developed nation by 2047, PM Modi drew a parallel with the importance of deadlines in journalism. He also thanked journalists for attending the gathering despite their busy schedules during the festive season, describing it as a “non-breaking news event”.The event was hosted by BJP president Nitin Nabin and attended by Union home minister Amit Shah, defence minister Rajnath Singh and health minister JP Nadda.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi recalled how a group of journalists once informed him that he had become the chief minister of Gujarat. He said the media played an important role in keeping democracy vibrant and added that “nothing is impossible in journalism’ PM Modi urged media organisations to highlight India's achievements and success stories.

Article Title: The Australian in Indira's Tihar compound: When Sonia Gandhi carried lunch for Charles Sobhraj's accomplice
Article Text:
"My mother-in-law felt sorry for her," Sonia writes (Photo: PTI).

NEW DELHI: On Christmas Day 1978, Sonia Gandhi carried a home-cooked lunch into Tihar Jail for her imprisoned mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi , and, at the former Prime Minister's request, enough extra for a young Australian woman she describes as the accomplice of serial killer Charles Sobhraj.The episode appears in Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi's memoir, released on November 10. It is set in the week Indira Gandhi spent in Tihar after the Janata Party , the combined opposition formation, came to power in the elections that followed the Emergency. Sonia writes that she visited the jail daily during that period.Also Read| When Sonia Gandhi carried lunch to Tihar for Charles Sobhraj's accomplice Christmas, she recalls, had always been a special day in the household, especially for the children, even when Sanjay and Rajiv were little boys. "The celebration had no religious meaning for us, but it was a festive day when we exchanged gifts and decorated the house with colourful baubles and red poinsettias," she writes."But on this Christmas my mother-in-law was in jail. I felt that I had to do something special to keep our spirits up."A friend offered to send sliced ham with roast potatoes and a small Christmas pudding, while Sonia would prepare "a good soup and some vegetables".The plan soon had to expand."At my mother-in-law's request, the food had to be enough also for the three women who took turns guarding her and a young woman prisoner in her compound," Sonia writes. She identifies the prisoner as "an Australian girl, the accomplice of the dreaded Charles Sobraj, convicted for multiple murders of young tourists in Thailand, Nepal, and India"."My mother-in-law felt sorry for her," Sonia writes.Then came a hitch. "When it turned out that she didn't eat ham, we quickly had to change the menu and prepare a roast chicken instead."There was resistance from within the jail as well. The day before, Indira Gandhi had sent a note saying that "under no circumstances" should her daughter-in-law deliver lunch. Sonia was to have her Christmas meal with Rajiv and the children."I couldn't do it," she writes.She went to Tihar with the food, a book as a small gift, and cards from the children. "I rushed back rather late, but satisfied that I could celebrate with her briefly and also have lunch with Rajiv and the children," she recalls."As it happened, she was released the next day and came home."The passage offers a rare domestic glimpse into one of the most dramatic periods of modern Indian politics: a former prime minister in jail, her daughter-in-law shuttling between kitchen and cell, and a Christmas lunch stretched to include guards and a fellow prisoner linked to a notorious killer.
Article Summary: The episode appears in Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi's memoir, released on November 10. It is set in the week Indira Gandhi spent in Tihar after the Janata Party came to power in the elections that followed the Emergency. Sonia writes that she visited the jail daily during that period.

Article Title: SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad
Article Text:
SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad

Irretrievable breakdown of marriage no divorce ground in Indian law: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking advantage of liberal laws abroad to obtain a divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law, Supreme Court has ruled.Viewing negatively the use in a foreign court of grounds for divorce which are not recognised in India, SC said a person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist under Indian law, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.With many men approaching a foreign court to get a divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage - despite the wife opposing the plea - and thereafter remarrying, SC said the person has to face proceedings even in a case where he had become a citizen of a foreign country. The top court said legal consequences stemm-ing from the subsisting marriage cannot be overridden by a subsequent change in a spouse's nationality.The bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar allowed criminal proceedings for bigamy against a man who remarried after getting a divorce order from a foreign court on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage in proceedings opposed by the wife.The court said that irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a ground for divorce in Indian law and, therefore, the divorce granted by the foreign court is not valid.“In our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily. This violates the legal threshold of Section 13 of the CPC, which every foreign decree has to pass through,” the SC bench said.The bench also said that if the foreign decree does not satisfy the requirements of Section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code, then the husband, relying on such a decree, cannot be permitted to contend that his first marriage stood dissolved in the eyes of matrimonial laws of India and, thus, escape the rigours of Section 494 of IPC (marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife).“Now, coming to the argument of the husband that since he was a British citizen when the second marriage with second wife was solemnised and since the second marriage took place outside India, keeping in view the mandate of Section 4 of the IPC, he cannot be held liable. We cannot accept this submission in the manner canvassed as the husband was married to first wife in India under Hindu rites, rituals and customs; thus, even if the second marriage took place outside India, the allegations under Section 494 of the IPC cannot be said to be diluted since enquiry for the offence of bigamy cannot be confined to the place of second marriage but must necessarily take into account the subsisting matrimonial relationship. ..” the bench said.The court, however, quashed criminal proceedings against the parents and second wife of the man.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law. A person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai India's cleanest city, Indore's domination ends
Article Text:

Survey: Rudrapur is cleanest Himalayan city

NEW DELHI: Navi Mumbai bagged the cleanest city award in the 10th edition of Centre's annual cleanliness survey, marking a change at the top after Indore dominated for eight consecutive years. Surat and Vijayawada were ranked the second and third cleanest cities, while Madhya Pradesh's Rewa was declared the cleanest riverfront town and Uttarakhand's Rudrapur emerged as the cleanest Himalayan city.President Droupadi Murmu conferred the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26. Madhya Pradesh led the states by winning nine awards at the national level for its cities under the cleanliness and sanitation category. Indore, which was so far the cleanest city, was placed in a different category this year, securing second position in the Mentor City category along with its partner town Depalpur, under the newly introduced 'Swachh Shehar Jodi' initiative.Greater Visakhapatnam secured the first position, followed by Jabalpur and Lucknow, among cities with population of more than 10 lakh, under the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26.Among cities with a population of 50,000 to three lakh, Dewas got the top rank, followed by New Delhi Municipal Council and Sagar.Vita in Maharashtra topped the 20,000-50,000 population category.Minister Manohar Lal said the full list of scores will be out soon. The survey also recognised cities for their performance in specialised categories. MP’s Rewa topped the cleanest riverfront towns category, followed by Bilaspur and Varanasi. In the Swachh Coastal Town category, Odisha’s Puri secured the first position. While Rudrapur was the cleanest Himalayan city, Jammu secured the second rank.
Article Summary: Navi Mumbai is India's cleanest city, Indore's domination ends. Surat and Vijayawada were ranked the second and third cleanest cities. Madhya Pradesh's Rewa was declared the cleanest riverfront town. Uttarakhand's Rudrapur emerged as cleanest Himalayan city.

Article Title: Collegium wants transfer of HC judges streamlined, random ways discarded
Article Text:
Collegium wants transfer of HC judges streamlined, random ways discarded

Judge ‘close to’ CJI runs transfer risk once mentor leaves office

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court collegium is trying to break away from the unwritten norms for transfer of judges from one high court to another, done so far on the basis of a judge's integrity, conduct, requirement of expertise in another HC and, very often, because of his/her closeness to an ex-CJI or ex-collegium member.The five-member SC collegium led by CJI Surya Kant and comprising Justices Vikram Nath, B V Nagarathna, M M Sundresh and P S Narasimha had an informal discussion last week on evolving a well-defined policy framework to streamline the process for transfer of judges from their parent HC to another. They felt that random or pick-and-choose methods of transfer for reasons that are not objective must be discarded. A proposal for transfer of a judge from his/her parent HC to another could be moved for various reasons.For instance, an HC judge, high in seniority, could be transferred to prepare him/her for taking over as CJ of that HC. There have also been occasions when a senior judge was sent to another HC to create a buffer between the CJ and senior judges there because they were not getting along.There have been cases where transfer proposals were initiated when in-house inquiries corroborated complaints regarding the integrity of a judge or that his/her behaviour was unbecoming of the constitutional post in the courtroom or in public.On the constructive side, a judge having expertise in certain fields of litigation could be transferred to another HC where his/her services could be more productive.There is another reason as well, one that has never made it to the records but has always been whispered aloud, a secret that is hardly so — a judge perceived to be close to a CJI or a member of the SC collegium who is transferred as soon as the mentor has demitted office. Very often, it is meant to settle scores against the CJI who refused to accommodate requests for appointment or transfer of judges from colleagues. All these grounds for transfers till 2018 were couched in the specious “in the interest of better administration of justice” officialese.The phraseology was discarded by 2020 and collegium resolutions plainly stated the transfer of a particular judge.In 2022, the collegium had recommended transfers of 18 HC judges, 34 in 2023, 11 in 2024, 44 in 2025 and 12 in 2026. The deliberations among members of the SC collegium would factor in the complexities and may also include a provision for reconsideration of a recommendation for transfer which has not been honoured by the executive.There have been some examples where recommendations for transfers remained pending for years with govt. In some cases, the collegium had acted expeditiously in accepting representations of HC judges seeking transfers while in others, it had maintained a posture of benign indifference.Even though SC has frowned upon transfers being used as a punitive measure, the majority of transfers in the past five years were seen as dislodging judges from their parent HCs because of one or the other complaint.A view has gained ground that in such situations, the judge concerned should be asked by the CJ concerned to mend his/her ways within a specified period before the collegium resorts to shifting him/her out.
Article Summary: The five-member SC collegium led by CJI Surya Kant had an informal discussion last week on evolving a well-defined policy framework. They felt that random or pick-and-choose methods of transfer for reasons that are not objective must be discarded.

Article Title: Canada envoy signals major breakthrough in ties with likely conclusion of trade talks by PM visit next month
Article Text:
Canada's high commissioner to India Christopher Cooter.

Addressing student concerns

Normalisation far beyond a reset, Modi hailed "fastest acceleration"

Internal Security, Khalistan Extremism & the Nijjar Investigation

Navigating trade volatility & US midterms

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Carney's return visit in January?

As they hold the 6th round of trade negotiations this week, Canada's high commissioner to India Christopher Cooter has said Ottawa is confident of finalising the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) ahead of PM Narendra Modi's visit to Canada next month.While the agreement will still have to be ratified, the announcement about successful conclusion of the negotiations during Modi's December 11-12 visit will mark a major milestone in the relationship, capping the dramatic turnaround in India-Canada ties under Canadian PM Mark Carney and Modi in the past 18 months. The relationship nosedived in 2023 after Canada alleged Indian state involvement in the killing of Sikh separatist and Canadian national Hardeep Singh Nijjar."The actual ratification would take some time because we have provincial governments that are involved as well. It's only legal when it's ratified on both sides. But I think we can be pretty confident that the final text will be there," said Cooter in an interaction with senior TOI editors."We are hopeful about our ratification process. The 6th round of talks is coming up. I'm pretty confident that we're getting close, so we'll keep our fingers crossed.We're also looking at some subsidiary agreements that would facilitate business travel," added Cooter. He also said many other big-ticket announcements were expected from the visit including in space.The high commissioner also addressed public anxiety over international student policies of Canada, home to the largest number of Indian students at roughly 300,000. He clarified that official caps were targeted at fraudulent institutions rather than legitimate Indian applicants."It's not so much the caps as the thought about the caps. People said, oh my God, Canada's not open. This was a misperception. In fact, the caps are nowhere near being met. This is probably the best time ever, if you're a prospective Indian student, to apply. Of course there were some abuses. There were these fly-by-night colleges. They weren't about education as much as getting PR status. So, we've got to clean that up, which is why the numbers will come down some. But it's still very, very significant," said Cooter.Beyond traditional student migration, according to Cooter, Canada is looking at a shift towards joint degree offerings, institutional presence in India, and mutually beneficial mobility frameworks.Cooter also said that the progress witnessed in the relationship since Carney assumed office had moved far beyond a reset. He said that the recovery was initially fragile, but gained unprecedented momentum following bilateral engagements between the leaders."It's not a reset. It is far beyond a reset. When I arrived here in September of last year, it was a tentative approach. None of us knew what was going to happen next. Is this going to be a slow march? Are we going to take a step back? Very fragile at the beginning. But it didn't happen that way. When the Foreign Minister (Anita Anand) was here last month, we called on your Prime Minister and he described it as the fastest acceleration he had ever experienced in a relationship," said Cooter.He stressed that both governments were looking to build institutional economic and societal interdependencies that make the overall bilateral relationship resilient to any potential future political disagreements."The idea is to have so much momentum, so much ballast in your ship going forward that it can't vary, that we'll have ups and downs politically. There'll be economic ups and downs and so forth, but we'll have such a weight of economic and institutional linkages that this process kind of goes forward on its own, as it should do between two economies, two societies that are so naturally partners," he said.As about pending requests for extradition of India-designated Khalistanis, Cooter said Ottawa is examining everything that India has brought to its attention but also stressed that Canada's legal system works in a way that's different from India."Evidentiary standards are different... nobody is blocking anything for political reasons. We're moving as much as possible within the systems that we've got...respecting the rights. Obviously, we've got to maintain evidentiary standards and other things under our charter of rights as under your laws," said the high commissioner, recalling a report by Canadian intelligence to Parliament earlier this year that spoke about Khalistanis who espouse violence.Cooter mentioned the recent meetings between the National Security Advisors this year while talking about increasing security cooperation and said what was a very negative kind of relationship had become quite positive."There are now linkages that are in place that allow people to basically pick up the phone or WhatsApp and be in touch with each other. We have adopted a position of no surprises as much as possible," he said.Asked about the status of the probe into the Nijjar killing, Cooter stated the matter was in court and judicial proceedings are thickly insulated from the political system. After the US Department of Justice indicted Lawrence Bishnoi and his aide for ordering the hit on Nijjar, Canadian authorities had said that the American investigations had not yielded any evidence to link the Indian government with the June 2023 shooting."It's slowly going through the courts. The evidence is before the courts, and it's moving forward in a system that's entirely independent of what the government does. So, we'll see where that ends up," he said.Asked about the US Congress flip and its likely impact for Canada and India as they negotiate trade deals with Washington, Cooter stated tariffs don't help people and affordability had become an issue in the US."It's early days, a division of powers and Mr. Trump has a lot of power, whether Congress is Democrat or Republican. There are some strands within the Democratic Party that line up to some extent with the Republican Party. You can think of China, for example, as one area where there's quite a bit of alignment between the two parties. What we heard before the midterms was actually somewhat encouraging. There were signs from Washington of more openness to start negotiating the game more seriously with Canada," said Cooter.Cooter said that global trade volatility reinforces why both Canada and India must deepen bilateral and multilateral partnerships across the Indo-Pacific and beyond, regardless of political shifts in Washington."I think, as I'm sure India also believes, rightly or wrongly, nobody wants to have too many eggs in one basket. And in fact, we are not going to depart from the path we have chosen over the last few months.And that's evident in the budget (tabled November 5) and where we relocated our funds yesterday. We also have a new national security strategy. We're going to rebuild our armed forces. We'll have more capability. We've got to deal with things like the Arctic. .. that's not going to change whether the Americans get a deal with us on trade or not. And frankly, that makes us a better partner for the US anyway," said Cooter.On whether Carney would visit India in January for the Republic Day, Cooter underlined that for Ottawa substance will determine whether back-to-back visits can take place. "I certainly would be telling the Prime Minister we would love to have you back. I'm sure India would too. But we want to be able to make enough progress following this summit so that...it would be largely symbolic if he comes back in 1 month, which is good. But we'd like to have lots of substance," said Cooter, adding he wasn't aware of any invitation to Carney yet for the Republic Day.
Article Summary: Canada's high commissioner to India Christopher Cooter said Ottawa is confident of finalising the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) ahead of PM Narendra Modi's visit to Canada next month. Cooter also addressed public anxiety over international student policies of Canada, home to the largest number of Indian students at roughly 300,000.

Article Title: Ex-VP Jagdeep Dhankhar collapses during morning walk, admitted to AIIMS
Article Text:
Dhankhar has been placed under the care of AIIMS cardiologists following a health emergency on Wednesday morning

NEW DELHI: Former Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar was taken to AIIMS hospital in New Delhi on Wednesday after he collapsed during his morning walk and briefly lost consciousness, news agency PTI reported citing sources.The 75-year-old was initially taken home by security personnel accompanying him in a police control room (PCR) vehicle.An ILBS medical team and AIIMS doctor attended to him and provided medical assistance. However, considering his health condition, he was later shifted to AIIMS in an ambulance.Dhankhar has been admitted to the hospital's cardio-neuro centre, where doctors from the cardiology department are conducting his medical evaluation and treatment. His health condition was not immediately known. AIIMS authorities have not issued an official statement so far.This is not the first time Dhankhar has experienced a medical emergency. In March 2025, he was admitted to AIIMS's critical care unit after complaining of chest pain and subsequently underwent angioplasty.He also fainted during the golden jubilee celebrations of Kumaon University in Nainital in June 2025. In January this year, he reportedly lost consciousness twice at his residence while heading to the washroom.Dhankhar served as the country's 14th vice-president from August 2022 until July 21, 2025, when he resigned from the post.
Article Summary: Former Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar was taken to AIIMS hospital in New Delhi on Wednesday after he collapsed during his morning walk. In a season crowded with big releases, one small film is quietly building big word-of-mouth. Enemy of the Smuggler, written and directed by IRS officer T. Samaya Murali, is being celebrated by audiences as a complete mass entertainer - a film that combines real customs investigations, high-stakes smuggling, family emotion, action, and suspense in equal measure.Released in cinemas worldwide on 30th October 2026, the film has now entered its second week with steady footfalls, especially from family audiences and youth. Leading media houses are calling it "Super Smart", "gripping" and "worthwhile watch."What makes the response particularly compelling is the man behind it. Samaya Murali is no conventional commercial filmmaker. An Indian Revenue Service officer who has served in Customs, he has witnessed smuggling cases firsthand. It is this real-world experience that audiences say lends the film its authenticity and sets it apart."It doesn't feel like a film made from imagination. It feels like it was made from real files," said a Chennai audience member after a weekend show. "Every raid, every interrogation, every trick the smugglers use - it felt real. That is why it connects."Enemy of the Smuggler revolves around a dedicated customs officer who takes on a powerful smuggling syndicate operating through ports and cargo shipments.The film follows the cat-and-mouse game between the officer and the smugglers, from container inspections and port intelligence to undercover operations and high-voltage confrontations.At its core, however, it is not just about smuggling. It is about society, what forces youngsters to take up smuggling, why India is being targeted by the drug smuggling cartels. While in majority of the real cases, main persons involved escape and only the small people directly involved get caught, this film shows how the main person involved is caught cleverly by the customs officer.This blend of realism and commercial cinema is what the audience has embraced.said another viewer in Madurai.The most praised aspect of the film has been Samaya Murali's direction.Critics and audiences alike have noted that his writing is tight, his staging of investigation sequences is authentic, and his ability to build suspense without losing emotional connection is impressive for a debut director from a non-film background.His IRS background brings a level of detail rarely seen in Tamil cinema. How customs intelligence works, how a container is flagged, how smugglers use legal loopholes, and how officers work under pressure with limited resources.said a film buff after a show in Coimbatore.The film's reception in the Tamil and English press has further strengthened its run.Kumudam called the film "Super Smart", Dinakaran gave it 3 Stars and praised it as "Solid Action & Gripping Story", while Dinathanthi described it as "Nari Vettai - Intense Thriller."In English media, Chennaivisionrated it 3.6/5 and called it a "Worthwhile Watch", News Today gave it 3 stars for being "A Gripping Crime Thriller", MyKollywooddescribed it as "A Promising Customs Smuggling Thriller", and Hello Madras noted that it is "a gripping crime thriller that brings customs investigation to screen."IMDb users have rated it 9.4/10 describing it as "Suspenseful & Gritty", while the overall audience rating stands at 3.5/5, with family audiences driving repeat viewership.One of the biggest surprises of the film's run has been its family audience acceptance.Unlike many thrillers that rely on excess violence or vulgarity, Enemy of the Smuggler has been positioned as a clean family entertainer. There are no unnecessary diversions. The focus remains on story, investigation, and emotion.Families, especially those who have members in government service, police, and customs, have related strongly to the protagonist's struggle - fighting a system much larger than himself.said a young viewer in Trichy.On social media, the phrase "mass entertainer" has been trending among fans of the film. Theatre videos show audiences cheering for the interval block, the raid sequences, and the climax confrontation.Exhibitors report that evening and night shows in Chennai, Madurai, Coimbatore, and Trichy have seen stronger occupancy over the first weekend, driven largely by word-of-mouth and not just opening-day publicity.Trade observers say this is a classic example of content-driven success, a film with a fresh subject, honest making, and strong audience connection finding its audience slowly but steadily.What's next?With positive talk continuing, the team behind Enemy of the Smuggler is now planning to expand shows and promote the film further across Tamil Nadu and overseas markets where Tamil audiences are strong.For Samaya Murali, the response is both humbling and encouraging. "I wanted to show the world what Customs officers actually go through - the intelligence, the risk, the sacrifice. If audiences are calling it a mass entertainer while also understanding that world, then my purpose is served," he said in a recent interaction.Enemy of the Smuggler is now running successfully in theatres across Tamil Nadu.
Article Summary: Enemy of the Smuggler is being celebrated by audiences as a complete mass entertainer. Written and directed by IRS officer T. Samaya Murali, the film combines real customs investigations, high-stakes smuggling, family emotion, action, and suspense in equal measure.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: Why was Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart ejected? All about clash with Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey
Article Text:
Marcus Smart. Image via: youngamechanger/ Instagram

Why was Marcus Smart ejected from the Warriors game?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Smart Finishes with six points in 16 minutes for Houston

Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart was ejected from Wednesday night’s game against the Golden State Warriors after throwing a punch at Warriors center Charles Bassey. It happened with 21 seconds left in the third quarter, right after Amen Thompson scored on a three-point play in transition. Houston was ahead at the time. Smart and Bassey went face-to-face at the top of the key, and his right hand seemed to fall just short of Bassey’s face. The two were pulled apart. Smart stormed off to the locker room, and officials eventually ruled him out.Officials went to the NBA Replay Center in Secaucus, New Jersey, to look at the clash between Marcus Smart and Charles Bassey. They came back with a Flagrant 2 on Smart. The call covers contact judged unnecessary and excessive. A Flagrant 1 would have brought the same two free throws and possession for the offended team, but Smart would have stayed in the game. The Flagrant 2 added the ejection. So Golden State got two free throws and the ball, while Houston lost its guard on the same play.Smart did not wait for the verdict. He was already off the floor while officials sorted it out, and ESPN analyst Doris Burke had no doubt how it would end. “You didn’t even need to tell him, he knew he was gone,” Burke said during the broadcast.She added, “That’s absolutely a punch.”Bassey stayed in the game, so the penalty landed on the Rockets guard alone. The play also put Bassey in an odd spot. He was part of the exchange yet stayed in the game, and Golden State kept its center on the floor for the rest of the night. One call was enough. Another technical or flagrant foul was never needed.Smart’s night ended with six points and two rebounds in 16 minutes. Houston entered the fourth with a lead to hold and one fewer guard to hold it. Teammates had to cover the minutes Smart would have played. The exchange also pulled attention away from the basketball Houston needed to play with a lead on the line.A Flagrant 2 settles the penalty inside the game and does not automatically bring a suspension. Any further discipline would be a separate league decision.
Article Summary: Houston Rockets guard Marcus Smart was ejected from Wednesday night’s game against the Golden State Warriors after throwing a punch at Warriors center Charles Bassey. The incident happened with 21 seconds left in the third quarter, right after Amen Thompson scored on a three-point play in transition. The call covers contact judged unnecessary and excessive.

US Soccer's ambitious pursuit of Guardiola

United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino acknowledges supporters after the World Cup round of 16 soccer match between the United States and Belgium in Seattle, Monday, July 6, 2026. (AP Photo/Ted S. Warren)

Guardiola's record makes him an ambitious target

FILE - Manchester City's head coach Pep Guardiola, right, and Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak celebrate with the Premier League trophy after the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and West Ham United at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, England, Sunday, May 19, 2024. Manchester City clinched the English Premier League on Sunday after beating West Ham in their last match of the season. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson, File)

Mauricio Pochettino's future with the USMNT could have major implications for the federation's next managerial appointment. With Manchester United reportedly identifying the Argentine as a leading candidate, US Soccer may have an opportunity to pursue a long-standing ambition: bringing Pep Guardiola into international football.Pochettino has emerged as Manchester United's preferred candidate to replace Michael Carrick should the club decide to make a managerial change, according to The Athletic. The possibility has prompted US Soccer to consider its options, with sources familiar with the federation's thinking telling the outlet that Guardiola would be a leading target if the Argentine departs.Carrick's position has come under pressure following a difficult start to the campaign. Despite receiving a two-year permanent contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish as interim manager, he has overseen the club's poorest domestic start in 40 years.United's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday left them 18th in the Premier League, with just one win and eight points from their opening 10 matches. They have also been eliminated from the League Cup and sit 17th in the Champions League standings, while reported frustrations from senior players, including captain Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez, have added to the pressure surrounding Carrick.Pochettino, meanwhile, remains in charge of the USMNT and was leading preparations for the team's Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti as of Wednesday. He is expected to oversee those fixtures, regardless of the speculation surrounding his future.Guardiola has already been discussed internally across multiple levels of US Soccer's recruitment process, according to sources cited by The Athletic. However, persuading the Spaniard to take charge would be a considerable challenge, particularly because he has shown little indication that he intends to return to management immediately after leaving Manchester City this summer.The former City manager turned down the opportunity to take charge of Italy earlier this year. Italian football federation president Giovanni Malago later discussed their approach in an interview with“Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us,” Malago said.Guardiola’s connection with the United States dates back to 2012, when he moved to New York with his family after leaving Barcelona and spent a year away from football, living in a luxury apartment overlooking Central Park. He enjoyed a degree of anonymity during that sabbatical.He has also previously expressed interest in the possibility of working with the US national team. Speaking in September 2024, shortly after Pochettino's appointment, Guardiola said he had friends in the country and believed the programme had considerable potential.“The USA is fascinating to try to build a project for many years and being able to get the national team to the next step,” he said. “The potential with the USA is there for the amount of people and sports and so on.”US Soccer's interest in Guardiola predates the current situation. Former federation president Sunil Gulati has a longstanding relationship with the Spaniard and was among those who first suggested that he might one day consider coaching the national team.The federation explored that possibility during its search following the 2022 World Cup, while Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp were also contacted at the beginning of the recruitment process that eventually brought Pochettino to the United States in 2024.US Soccer even approached wealthy donors to help finance the salary required to attract a high-profile international manager. Guardiola, Klopp and Pochettino were identified as three candidates whose reputations and experience made them suitable for the position.The federation would now have a potential four-month window to conduct another search after the current international commitments. The USMNT is expected to hold a largely domestic-based training camp in December outside a FIFA international window, with its next competitive matches scheduled for March.That timetable could offer Guardiola additional time before a possible return to coaching, although there is no indication that he has agreed to take the job or that negotiations have begun.Guardiola would bring an exceptional managerial record to the national team. Across Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City, he has won three Champions League titles, six Premier League championships, three La Liga titles and three Bundesliga titles.His decade at City brought six league titles, three FA Cups, five League Cups and the club's first Champions League triumph. Before arriving in England, he won the Bundesliga in each of his three seasons at Bayern, having established his reputation at Barcelona with three league titles and two Champions League trophies in four seasons.His achievements at City, however, have faced scrutiny following the club's financial-regulations case, in which City was found guilty on nearly all the charges it faced.For US Soccer, Guardiola would represent an ambitious appointment ahead of the next phase of the national team's development. But much depends on whether Pochettino actually leaves for Manchester United, and whether Guardiola is willing to end his break from management.
Article Summary: Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as Manchester United's preferred candidate to replace Michael Carrick, according to The Athletic. The possibility has prompted US Soccer to consider its options, with sources familiar with the federation's thinking telling the outlet that Guardiola would be a leading target if the Argentine departs. US Soccer's interest in Guardiola predates the current situation.

Article Title: 'If Neeraj Chopra can, why can't I?': National record holder Nirbhay Chaudhary on his Olympic dream
Article Text:
Nirbhay Chaudhary (Image credit: Special arrangement)

The wall of inspiration: From 70m + to 75m

Nirbhay Chaudhary (Image credit: Special arrangement)

71.02m is not enough: A long way to go

Nirbhay Chaudhary (Image credit: Special arrangement)

Nirbhay's Olympic dreams

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: "Maine waha se start kiya hai jaha se log finish karte hain [I have started where others finish]" - that is how hammer thrower Nirbhay Chaudhary looks at his national record-breaking performance. He threw 71.02m at the Indian Athletics Series Final this October, breaking a national record that had stood for almost 10 years.His throw erased the previous record of 70.73m, set by Neeraj Kumar in 2016.Despite the record, Nirbhay was not fully satisfied with his effort. After releasing the hammer, he initially thought of stepping out of the circle so that the throw would not be counted. However, he changed his mind.A few moments later, he heard the noise around him. When he asked his coach what had happened, he was told that he had broken the national record."I had made that throw casually. I did not think it would be a record-breaking effort. I had not even used much power. I never expected the hammer to travel so far or that I would break the national record. I don't know how it went that far," Nirbhay told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.For Nirbhay, whose name means 'fearless', the national record is only the beginning. He now wants to cross 75m and eventually reach the 80m mark."This is just the beginning. I am really proud of this performance. It has given me a new beginning. I have started where others finish," he said.A few months ago, Nirbhay returned to his room after a tiring practice session. He was covered in sweat, but the session had not gone as planned. He was struggling to perform, and his body was getting tired quickly as he recovered from dengue.His family was also worried about his future in athletics. Frustrated and angry, Nirbhay picked up a marker and wrote a target on the wall beside his bed: "70 + national record". He also set a deadline for himself - September 10. He then prepared a training schedule and followed it closely. His routine included waking up early, cleaning his hammer, stretching, working out, running and practising his throws with full power.He achieved his target on the date he had set. After breaking the national record, he crossed out 70m on the wall and replaced it with 75m."I have crossed out 70 and written 75. I will achieve that target too. It is true that there is no substitute for hard work. I believe in that. I am also stubborn. When I work hard with determination, I get what I want. I will continue to do that," Nirbhay said.He revealed that he had written the target on the wall last year, when he was going through a difficult phase."I had written it last year. I was very frustrated at that time. My family was also worried because my physical condition had become very poor. Everyone was asking me to continue with the sport, even if I could only do a little."I know what condition I was in. And it has taken a year for this to happen. But the happiness I feel now cannot be bought. The feeling is surreal. But I won't stop," he said.Nirbhay believes one more season of hard work can help him make a big jump in his performance."I just need one more season. I can achieve a big mark after that. 75m is my main target right now, and then I want to reach 80m. It will require a lot of hard work, but I am sure I will be able to do it," he said.Nirbhay knows that 71.02m is not enough to compete at the biggest international events. Even though his throw was above the Asian Games qualification mark of 69.12m, he missed the opportunity to compete at the Asian Games because of the timing of the qualification process and the deadlines involved."Practice was going on. The qualification issue was actually about dates. It depends on the host country. If the host sends an invitation or agrees to accommodate you, then things can be worked out, even if you are late. But there is a deadline for everything."There is a fixed time for it. By the time that deadline passed, I was not competing. I was only preparing for practice and other things. I had not even thought about whether I would go or not. We could not make a decision in time, so it did not happen. I could not go," he said.Nirbhay believes Indian hammer throw needs to improve its standards. While athletes in other events have raised their levels, he wants to bring the same change to hammer throw."I feel I can take hammer throw forward in India. We need to change things. Neeraj (Chopra) bhai has set an example for everyone in javelin. I want to do the same in hammer throw. He first crossed 70m, then 80m, 85m and now 90m. I want to achieve similar milestones in hammer throw," Nirbhay said."The standard of hammer throw in India has been very low for a long time. I want to raise that standard. I also want other athletes who are currently behind to reach that level. I want to see more youngsters take up hammer throw as a career and more athletes come into the event," he said.India has never had an Olympic medal in hammer throw. The country has also had very few representatives in the event at the Games.Somnath Chopra represented India at the 1948 Summer Olympics and finished 23rd in the qualifying round. Erman Bastian represented India at the 1960 Summer Olympics but did not start his event.Praveen Kumar Sobti, who later became famous for playing Bheem in the television series Mahabharat, represented India at the 1968 Summer Olympics. He finished 20th in the qualifying round.India has won five medals in hammer throw at the Asian Games, including two silver and three bronze. Somnath Chopra and Kishen Singh won silver and bronze respectively at the 1951 Games. Praveen Kumar added another bronze in 1966, while Nirmal Singh Grewal won silver in 1974. Manju Bala was India's most recent hammer throw medallist, winning bronze at the 2014 Asian Games.India has won just one hammer throw medal in Commonwealth Games history. Praveen Kumar Sobti won silver at the 1966 Commonwealth Games in Kingston.For Nirbhay, breaking the national record is only the first step. He wants to take Indian hammer throw to a higher level and believes the country can win an Olympic medal in the event. The Olympic qualification mark for the 2028 Los Angeles Games is 78.50m."Why can't we win an Olympic medal? As I said, we need to set an example. I can be that example. I really want to put hammer throw on India's map of Olympic medal-winning events. India can win an Olympic medal in hammer throw. We just need one example, one athlete who achieves something big. After that, the path will become easier for others."Now I have almost all the facilities I need. I get support from the Athletics Federation and SAI. My coaches, including Naval Singh, have given their best. I have the equipment and everything else I need. So I will do it. I believe in myself. I will achieve this," he said.
Article Summary: Nirbhay Chaudhary threw 71.02m at the Indian Athletics Series Final this October. His throw erased the previous record of 70.73m, set by Neeraj Kumar in 2016. He now wants to cross 75m and eventually reach the 80m mark.

A ruling meant to simplify inheritance ended up at the heart of a family property dispute, with a Pennsylvania mother and daughter on opposite sides of a hefty financial disagreement. A shared property arrangement became a matter of ownership, sale proceeds and the division of money after a house was sold for $262,519. The Pennsylvania Superior Court’s upholding of separate financial awards for both women has now closed an important chapter of the dispute.The dispute began in February 2010 when Carole Caples purchased property on South Fifth Street in Whitehall, Pennsylvania, to be closer to her family and to downsize from her Maryland home.According to the Pennsylvania Superior Court, Caples added her daughter Katherine Purcell as a joint tenant with right of survivorship to the deed. The arrangement was to facilitate the administration of the estate and to allow the property to be sold and the proceeds equally divided between her 3 daughters on her death.The court ruled that Caples did not intend to give Purcell an individual financial interest in the property.She had repaid the money Purcell had put down on the purchase from the proceeds of her home in Maryland. Caples also paid the bills and utilities on the property. But Purcell never lived there or contributed to its upkeep.That family arrangement was put under the microscope in 2018 when Caples decided to move into Fellowship Community, a continuing-care retirement community, after hip surgery and a hospital stay. To join, she had to pay about $203,000.Purcell agreed to lend her mother $192,850 with a repayment agreement of monthly instalments of $975.60 for 20 years. The agreement was formalized in a promissory note signed on 1 July 2018.Caples also sold the Whitehall property on October 18, 2018, for net proceeds of $262,519.75. Both of their names were on the deed, so at settlement, each woman received about $131,259.88.But the Pennsylvania Superior Court ruled the distribution didn’t reflect Caples’ grasp of why her daughter had been added to the deed. She thought the money would eventually be available to her and her estate.The row escalated when Purcell later ordered her mother to pay $100,000 toward the outstanding loan and deposit a further $30,850 into a joint account to cover future instalments.The court considered what happened to the money paid in for the monthly repayments. In January 2019, Purcell moved $28,528.39 from the joint account into a personal account she held with her husband.She also kept making monthly payments on the loan, while her sisters, Kimberly D’Alessandro and Christine Cullen, repeatedly asked for information about their mother’s finances and the outstanding debt.Things got even more complicated when Purcell’s power of attorney for her mother was revoked in February 2019. Her sisters stepped in to manage Caples’ affairs.The Pennsylvania Superior Court acknowledged that evidence presented at the six-day trial showed that Caples had suffered from declining memory and confusion during the relevant period. Her medical history and her dependence on Purcell were important in determining whether a confidential relationship existed between them.The dispute ultimately led to a series of consolidated legal proceedings, including allegations of breach of contract, fiduciary duty and mismanagement of corporate funds.The jury found that Purcell had breached her fiduciary duty regarding the proceeds from the sale of the house and awarded Caples $131,291.54. It also found that Caples had breached the loan agreement and awarded Purcell $61,973.06 plus interest.After adjustments and further calculation of interest, the trial court rendered judgments in favor of Caples for $168,107 and in favor of Purcell for $77,461.86.Both women contested parts of the result., but Pennsylvania Superior Court denied their respective appeals on November 5, 2026 in a decision affirming the judgments.Image Courtesy: istock
Article Summary: Carole Caples bought a house in Whitehall, Pennsylvania, to be closer to her family and to downsize from her Maryland home. Caples added her daughter Katherine Purcell as a joint tenant with right of survivorship to the deed. The arrangement was to facilitate the administration of the estate and to allow the property to be sold and the proceeds equally divided between her 3 daughters on her death. The court ruled that Caples did not intend to give Purcell an individual financial interest in the property.

Article Title: 'Mate, well done': Australia captain Mitch Marsh responds to Usman Khawaja's ball-tampering claims
Article Text:
Usman Khawaja

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What happened in the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal?

Australia captain Mitch Marsh chose not to discuss the Sandpapergate scandal on Thursday, saying his focus was on leading the team in the upcoming white-ball series against England rather than revisiting events in Cape Town eight years ago.Marsh faced the media in Perth, five days after former Australia teammate Usman Khawaja brought the ball-tampering controversy back into the spotlight. In his autobiography, Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian squad knew about the plan to use sandpaper to rough up the ball during the 2018 Test against South Africa.The incident led to lengthy bans for three Australian players and had a major impact on cricket in the country. In the eight years since, Cricket Australia, the team management and several players have rarely spoken about the controversy. Members of Australia's bowling group have rejected claims that the entire team knew about the plan to use sandpaper to help the ball swing through the air.When asked about the scandal at the start of his scheduled press conference, Marsh responded: “You hit a six off the first ball there, Mate, well done!” He then added: “Look, obviously there's been a bit of noise around this week and I respect that certain people have told their stories."“I'm not here to share mine today, I know that might sound weird, but it's a big week for us and it's an important time for this one-day (squad) and my sole focus has been on preparing for tomorrow.”The controversy has dominated cricket coverage this week and is expected to remain a talking point as the Australian summer gets underway.Australia and England begin their white-ball series in Perth on Friday, with three ODIs and five T20Is scheduled between the teams. Meanwhile, Australia Test captain Pat Cummins is set to address the controversy at a press conference in Sydney, hours before the opening match.Cummins said he had taken time to understand Khawaja's claims before responding. “Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week,” Cummins posted on X. “I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly.”Steve Smith and David Warner, who were Australia's captain and vice-captain at the time, were each handed 12-month bans by Cricket Australia following an investigation into the ball-tampering incident. Cameron Bancroft, who was caught using sandpaper on the ball during the Test match, received a nine-month ban.Smith and Warner returned to the Australian team in 2019. Smith continues to play Test cricket for the country and is preparing for a four-match series against New Zealand starting next month.
Article Summary: Australia captain Mitch Marsh chose not to discuss the Sandpapergate scandal. Marsh said his focus was on leading the team in the upcoming white-ball series against England. The incident led to lengthy bans for three Australian players and had a major impact on cricket.

Article Title: “Just adore him and I think he is the greatest”: How Jason and Travis Kelce turned two Chiefs fans' unusual requests into special memories with heartfelt gestures
Article Text:
Jason and Travis Kelce turned two Chiefs fans' unusual requests into special memories with heartfelt gestures(Image via Getty Images)

Jason Kelce and the ESPN crew answered Samantha Secord's unusual request

Travis Kelce signed another fan's prosthetic leg after reaching 100 touchdowns

An autograph from an NFL star can become a lifelong memory. For two Kansas City Chiefs fans, that memory came in an unusual way. Jason and Travis Kelce each signed a fan's prosthetic leg during separate Chiefs games, turning two unexpected requests into memorable moments. While Jason's interaction happened in October 2024, Travis followed a year later, giving another supporter a reason to remember her night at Arrowhead Stadium.The two incidents also showed a different side of the Kelce brothers. Beyond their NFL achievements, both took time to connect with supporters who wanted something more personal than a photograph or a signed football.The first incident took place on October 7, 2024, when the Chiefs hosted the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football. Samantha Secord, a Chiefs season-ticket holder from Omaha, travelled more than 184 miles to watch her team. This time, she had a special request: she wanted Jason Kelce to sign her prosthetic leg.Secord and her friends tried to get the ESPN crew's attention during the broadcast. Their efforts eventually worked when Scott Van Pelt noticed them and helped bring the leg to the crew. Jason and the other ESPN personalities signed it during a commercial break.Speaking to KCTV5 on October 10, 2024, Secord described the experience as "kind of mind-blowing." However, she still had one autograph in mind."My favorite player is Travis Kelce. I just adore him, and I think he is the greatest," she told KCTV5. "He is the one that I am absolutely looking forward to signing my leg."Her request carried a personal meaning. Secord lost her leg after a 2022 UTV accident that injured the lower half of her body. She also explained that watching Travis play and following his community work helped her during recovery.A year later, on October 27, 2025, Travis had his own memorable interaction with a Chiefs supporter. Kansas City defeated the Washington Commanders 28-7, and Kelce reached 100 career touchdown receptions, becoming only the fourth tight end in NFL history to achieve the milestone.After the game, a different female fan caught his attention by raising her prosthetic leg towards him. People around her helped pass it to the tight end, who signed it as the crowd cheered. ESPN shared the interaction on its TikTok page.The gesture came during a night when Kelce had plenty of reasons to celebrate. Speaking to Scott Van Pelt during ESPN's postgame interview, he joked about his longevity."I'm just the old lucky dog that's still able to do this thing," Kelce said. Patrick Mahomes also praised his longtime teammate after the victory, calling him the "true Chiefs Chief." Head coach Andy Reid highlighted Kelce's energy and continued contribution to Kansas City.The two incidents involved different fans, but they shared a similar moment of connection. Jason and Travis each took time to fulfil an unusual autograph request, giving two Chiefs supporters memories that went far beyond the game.
Article Summary: Jason and Travis Kelce each signed a fan's prosthetic leg during separate Chiefs games, turning two unexpected requests into memorable moments. The two incidents involved different fans, but they shared a similar moment of connection. Jason's interaction happened in October 2024, while Travis followed a year later, giving another supporter a reason to remember her night at Arrowhead Stadium.

Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov were involved in a physical altercation in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday, with videos of the incident circulating on social media.The incident took place at a hotel lobby ahead of an MMA event scheduled in Abu Dhabi this weekend. Usman, the younger brother of Dvalishvili's former opponent Umar Nurmagomedov, was seen approaching the Georgian fighter from behind before slapping him across the face.Dvalishvili is in Abu Dhabi to compete at Saturday's Real American Freestyle (RAF) event. He later posted a video on Instagram showing his bloodied face after the incident.Several videos of the confrontation were shared online, including one by former UFC lightweight champion Ilia Topuria, who is friends with Dvalishvili. After the initial slap, Dvalishvili attempted to go after Usman, leading to a fight involving members of both fighters' camps. At least six people were involved in the altercation.Dvalishvili alleged that he and a young friend were attacked while he was giving an interview in the hotel lobby."Was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend. Security was holding me - They kept kicking us when we were down like losers," Dvalishvili captioned the Instagram video showing him receiving treatment.In another video following the incident, Dvalishvili referred to Usman and his team as "snakes" and questioned their actions."What a sneaky way, guys," Dvalishvili says. "What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this? If you want to try, let's do it the real way."The confrontation is the latest development in the long-running rivalry between Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedov camp. Before defeating Umar in January 2025, Dvalishvili had called him "spoiled" and accused the Dagestani fighter of being disrespectful.The two camps were also involved in a brief altercation in July at another RAF event in Georgia.Both Dvalishvili and Umar are scheduled to compete at Saturday's RAF event. Dvalishvili will face former UFC title challenger Marlon Moraes, while Umar is set to wrestle former UFC champion Urijah Faber.

Article Title: Michael Carrick sacked as Manchester United head coach after just three wins in season
Article Text:
Manchester United's head coach Michael Carrick waves to supporters after his team lost the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth in Manchester, England, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach, bringing an end to his 10-month spell in charge of the club, The Telegraph reported.The 45-year-old's departure comes after several days of uncertainty over his future, with United already working on appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick continued to take training on Tuesday and Wednesday before arriving at the club's Carrington training ground on Thursday morning, where he was finally informed of the decision.The decision to sack Carrick was approved at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday involving co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.However, it had become clear late on Monday that Carrick was set to leave. United spent the following days working on a deal to bring in Pochettino, the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager who is currently in charge of the United States national team.Pochettino is set to take charge of a United side struggling in the Premier League and the Champions League . The club are third from bottom of the Premier League, one point behind 17th-placed Coventry, and sit 17th in the Champions League standings.Carrick was appointed in May on a contract running until 2028 after a successful spell as interim manager.He had guided United to Champions League qualification, winning 12 and drawing three of his 17 matches last season. However, he was unable to maintain that record in the current campaign.United have managed only three wins in all competitions this season, against Ipswich, Sabah and Roma at home. They came back from two goals down to earn a late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last Sunday. The team had also recovered to beat Roma, but the club's management decided that a change was necessary.Carrick's departure adds to the uncertainty surrounding United, where disagreements between senior players and club officials have also come into focus. Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick's tactics following a 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como, while Martinez criticised Wilcox.Since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club in 2013, United have appointed eight managers, including Ralf Rangnick, who served as interim manager for five months.Carrick is the second United head coach to be sacked in the same calendar year. Ruben Amorim was dismissed in January, making this the first time in the club's history that two head coaches have been removed within one calendar year.
Article Summary: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach. The 45-year- old's departure comes after several days of uncertainty over his future. United are already working on appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. The club are third from bottom of the Premier League, one point behind 17th-placed Coventry.

Article Title: Stephen Curry breaks silence on Ayesha’s controversial movie kissing scene in new video calling out podcasters
Article Text:
Stephen Curry addresses backlash over Ayesha’s movie kissing scene. Image via: Noah Graham/Getty Images for Eat. Learn. Play

Why did Stephen Curry call out podcasters over Ayesha Curry’s movie?

Jemele Hill points to a Hailee Steinfeld double standard

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Stephen Curry has responded to the criticism aimed at his wife, Ayesha Curry , over a kiss scene in her new film. The Golden State Warriors guard posted a 90-second Instagram video on Wednesday, calling out podcast hosts who spoke about her role in Second Chance Holiday. Gilbert Arenas, Nick Young and Emmanuel Acho were the three in the spotlight. The romantic comedy arrived on The Roku Channel on November 5, with Ayesha opposite Matthew Daddario in her first leading film role. LeSean McCoy also questioned the scene on a separate podcast.Stephen Curry said the noise usually does not bother him or Ayesha, but this round crossed a line. He felt the hosts were trying to shrink his wife’s accomplishments while turning her life into podcast material. The four-time NBA champion tied it to a wider issue, saying the talk shows how people view women and what they are allowed to do."You're trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife, and obviously leading podcast tapings and topics, and giving opinions on somebody else's wife. Who feels the need to want to have to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about," Steph shared on Instagram.Arenas, who began his career with Golden State, had called Ayesha the only blemish on Curry’s family life on his podcast.Young, who played with Curry on the 2018 title team, also joined the conversation. McCoy separately questioned her choice to film the kiss. "Maybe the apology can be as loud as y'all leading y'all shows with this topic," Steph continued, adding, "Appreciate the free pub."Curry rarely engages with criticism of his family. He said he tried to laugh this one off, but “something needs to be said.” In his view, the apology should be as loud as the shows that led with the topic. He closed by thanking the hosts for the free publicity and telling viewers to stream the film on Roku.Second Chance Holiday follows Chelsey, a dating expert who returns home after a run of holiday breakups and reconnects with her high school sweetheart. The kiss with Daddario became the talking point online. McCoy said on his podcast he respected it if the scene was not real. Ayesha answered the noise herself, writing that it was not even real and calling the critics annoying.Ayesha wanted to act before she married the Warriors guard, with childhood commercials and a Hannah Montana episode on her résumé, according to journalist Jemele Hill. Hill also pointed to Hailee Steinfeld, who is married to Bills quarterback Josh Allen and had an intimate scene with Michael B. Jordan in Sinners. Hill said the film drew no similar outrage, and she called the backlash against Ayesha rooted in misogyny.Ayesha also had a supporting role alongside Lindsay Lohan in Irish Wish, a 2024 Netflix romantic comedy. Golden State, joint-third in the West at 8-3, was set to open a five-game road trip against Houston on Wednesday night.
Article Summary: Stephen Curry responded to the criticism aimed at his wife, Ayesha Curry, over a kiss scene in her new film. The Golden State Warriors guard posted a 90-second Instagram video on Wednesday, calling out podcast hosts who spoke about her role. Gilbert Arenas, Nick Young and Emmanuel Acho were the three in the spotlight.

“Tai, tumhi parat kadhi yenaar





CHANDRAPUR: The ramshackle mud hut in a remote Chandrapur hamlet still stands as a grim reminder of the past as 71-year-old Mathurabai walked into her new concrete house a few feet away.On Wednesday, the brave tribal survivor of the 1972 custodial rape case that changed India’s rape laws and brought dignity to millions of survivors, had a familiar visitor in Neelam Gorhe, former legislative council deputy chairperson, who had vowed to give her a dignified life when she came to her doorstep exactly a year ago.Then the frail woman had whispered in Marathi --? (When will you come back?)”. Gorhe kept her promise and returned to Sindewahi taluka on Bhai Dooj and turned the special occasion into ‘Bahin Dooj’ with Mathura.“I have a sister but no brother. Then, why not celebrate a Bahin dooj with Mathura,” said Gorhe, crystallising a survivor and saviour relation into an eternal bond.The meeting turned emotional when Mathura broke down and collapsed on Gorhe’s lap as the Sena MLC formally inaugurated the new house, which Maharashtra govt had allotted under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana As Gorhe held her hands, she too struggled to hold back tears as a festive cheer ran through the drought-hit village.Gorhe spent time with Mathura, her family and two sons. She shared a meal of rice and ‘baigan bhaji’ with them, joined by other tribal women farmers and handed out ration and Diwali kits.“Mathura’s elder son has landed a job. We are looking for some placements for the younger one. We have a plan to pen down Mathura’s life, struggle and legal journey in a book,” said Gorhe.Now in her seventies, Mathura, a Gond tribal girl, had faced stigma and hardship for 54 years. Her case became a turning point for women’s rights, but her life remained difficult.Maharashtra govt took steps for her rehabilitation after a remark from former Chief Justice of India Bhushan R Gavai brought the forgotten case back into focus and TOI told her story to the world.Mathura was a young, orphaned tribal girl in 1972. She lived with her brother and worked as a domestic help. On March 26 that year, her brother went to Desaiganj police station in Gadchiroli to report that she had been kidnapped.Mathura was asked to stay at the station, where two policemen, head constable Tukaram and constable Ganpat, sexually assaulted her.The sessions court acquitted the policemen in 1974. Bombay High Court convicted them in 1976, but Supreme Court overturned the conviction in 1978. The verdict had triggered nationwide protests.An open letter by four law professors and a women’s movement led to the Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1983. The changes strengthened protection against custodial rape and shifted the burden of proof in such cases.
Article Summary: Former deputy chairpe​rson of Maharashtra Legislative Council, Neelam Gorhe, on Wednesday celebrated Diwali with Mathura, survivor of the 1972 custodial rape case. Gorhe turned the special occasion into ‘Bahin Dooj’ withMathura.

Article Title: Punjab-origin newlywed couple and brother-in-law killed in NZ crash; families seek repatriation
Article Text:
Gurpreet Singh (left), Sukhvir Kaur (centre) and Sukhdeep Singh (right) killed in New Zealand crash/Image: NZ Herald

A Punjab-origin newlywed couple and their brother-in-law were killed after a car crashed into a BurgerFuel restaurant in Takanini, South Auckland, on Sunday night.The victims were identified as Sukhdeep Singh, 33, his wife Sukhvir Kaur, 29, and Gurpreet Singh, 38. Daljit Singh, president of the Supreme Sikh Society, told RNZ that all three belonged to the same family and were living together in South Auckland.The couple had married six months ago, and the wife had arrived in New Zealand recently. Their relatives are now seeking to arrange the repatriation of all three bodies so they can perform the final rituals in their home country.The crash occurred when a vehicle struck the restaurant building on Great South Road, killing all three people. RNZ reported that the car was believed to have been speeding at more than 150 km/h.Singh said the victims' families had been informed of the deaths, but the parents of the brother-in-law were yet to receive the news. His brothers knew about his death and were waiting for confirmation of the repatriation arrangements before informing their parents.“Only his brothers know that he has died,” Singh told RNZ.He said the victim's brother was concerned that telling their parents before the body could be brought back to India would cause them considerable distress.“He said the less time they have, the better it is for them,” Singh said, explaining that a lengthy wait between receiving the news and the body's arrival could make the situation more difficult for the parents.The families are hoping to bring the bodies back as soon as possible to conduct the funeral rites. However, the cost of repatriation is a major concern, with Singh estimating the expenses at between NZ40,000 and NZ50,000.He said travelling to New Zealand would also be financially difficult for relatives based overseas. The Supreme Sikh Society is planning to set up a Givealittle fundraising page to help meet the repatriation costs and provide assistance to the families.Singh said the local Sikh community was mourning the deaths and wanted clarity on the circumstances that led to the crash. He added that community members were awaiting the findings of the police investigation.A police spokesperson told RNZ that formal identification procedures were still underway. The bodies would be released to the families after the process was completed.
Article Summary: Sukhdeep Singh, 33, his wife Sukhvir Kaur, 29, and Gurpreet Singh, 38, were killed in a car crash in South Auckland on Sunday night. The couple had married six months ago, and the wife had arrived in New Zealand recently. Their relatives are now seeking to arrange the repatriation of all three bodies so they can perform the final rituals.
