Article Title: Stopped for document check, man sets tempo ablaze, waves sword and black flag in east Delhi
Article Text:
Man sets own tempo ablaze after stopped for document check in Delhi





NEW DELHI: A man allegedly set his own tempo on fire after being stopped by traffic police for a document check near the Ghazipur border in east Delhi on Thursday morning.He was later seen waving a sword and a black flag amid the chaos, police sources said.The incident took place around 8.30am when traffic personnel stopped the mini-goods carrier and asked its driver to produce the vehicle documents, news agency PTI reported.Aggravated over being stopped, the man allegedly got out of the vehicle, produced an inflammable substance and set the tempo on fire, police sources said.A purported video of the incident shows the vehicle engulfed in flames, while the man is seen holding a sword and a black flag.He is also seen waving the weapon, disrupting traffic in the area, PTI reported.“A PCR call regarding a fire in a vehicle near Ghazipur Murga Mandi Toll Tax was received at Ghazipur police station. Police staff immediately reached the spot near West Vinod Nagar depot, where a tempo was found partially burnt. The vehicle was empty.“During the incident, one person, identified as Ghanender, 28, obstructed traffic briefly. He was immediately apprehended by the police staff, and normal traffic movement was restored,” a police statement read.Police added that an FIR had been registered and further investigation was underway.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Man allegedly set his own tempo on fire after being stopped by traffic police. Incident took place near the Ghazipur border in east Delhi on Thursday morning. He was later seen waving a sword and a black flag amid the chaos, police said.

Article Title: Personal stories highlight the struggles and triumphs of the queer community
Article Text:
Amrita Tripathi

Jyotsna Suri

Divya Suri Singh and Keshav Suri

Saurabh Kirpal

Cyril Feuillebois

Shovana Narayan

Rajeev Sethi

The evening also featured a performance by drag artist Hash Brownie





A collection of personal stories from queer team members was at the heart of a book launch in Delhi. Hospitality With A Heart, written by Amrita Tripathi, follows experiences of isolation, bullying and pressure to conform, while asking what it takes to create a workplace where everyone feels they belong. “When we kicked off this project, I expected to hear stories about DEI (diversity, equity and inclusion) and queer leadership. What I heard instead were often heart-rending stories of isolation, bullying, intense pressure to conform,” Tripathi said. She also spoke about the impact of everyday gestures, saying that being “called the right name and not being made to feel ‘other’ can transform someone’s entire life”. For Keshav Suri, that sense of belonging is at the heart of hospitality. “True inclusion is when you don’t have to leave a part of yourself at the door to be welcomed in,” he said.The launch opened with a welcome address by Jyotsna Suri, chairperson and managing director, The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group. This was followed by a panel discussion with Amrita Tripathi, Rithik Hukku, Shaurya and Shruti on empathy, inclusion and what hospitality means beyond service. The stories in the book come from team members who are now part of She Leads, the Aditya Nanda Scholarship, Project Prahari and Apna Heera, among them LGBTQIA+ persons, acid attack survivors, persons with disabilities and neurodivergent individuals.
Article Summary: Hospitality With A Heart, written by Amrita Tripathi, follows experiences of isolation, bullying and pressure to conform. The stories in the book come from team members who are now part of She Leads, the Aditya Nanda Scholarship, Project Prahari and Apna Heera.

Article Title: A literary evening with a festive twist
Article Text:
Sharmila Tagore and Rakhshanda Jalil

Aman Nath, Laila Tyabji and Salman Khurshid (l to r)

Saba Ali

William Dalrymple and Laila Tyabji

A

debut novelist at 63

Sanjoy Roy

Madhu Trehan

Kapil Sibal

Neelima Dalmia Adhar

When Delhi traffic joined the conversation

Tara Gandhi Bhattacharjee

Salma Sultan





It is not often that one sees Delhi's literary circle dressed in their festive best for a book launch. But with Diwali festivities in full swing, even a literary evening called for bringing out the satins, chiffons, organzas, Banarasis and brocades. The occasion was the launch of author Rakhshanda Jalil 's book The Aunts of Gangapur, which turned into a grand gathering of friends and familiar faces from Delhi's literary and cultural circles. And no one seemed more surprised by the scale of the celebration than the author herself, who admitted that such “grand” events were rare for her.“I've only ever had very modest book launches for all my various books at the IIC with tea and cookies. So this is really a grand affair, and I'm very grateful and quite overwhelmed, actually,” she said as she welcomed the gathering. The author added that she had envisioned the launch of this book as a celebration with her friends, who did turn up in good numbers.Introducing her book The Aunts Of Gangapur, Rakhshanda shared that she was a “debut novelist at 63”, having spent much of her writing career working on non-fiction, biographies and translations.“My métier has been non-fiction, literary non-fiction. I’ve written a clutch of rather boring books, biographies and translations and so on. So this is a leap of faith, something very new. I thought this book would be a fun way to talk about serious things. Serious things that get brushed under the carpet in the din of more politically vibrant issues. It’s located in the Gangetic heartland, an area that I’ve come to know and understand. But my one takeaway from this book, really, the writing of this book, really, is that age is just a number. I am a debut novelist at 63,” she said.While the book remained the focus of the evening, Delhi’s traffic managed to become a talking point of its own, with delayed arrivals and stories of getting stuck on the roads finding their way into conversations. Sharmila Tagore , who was among the guests invited to read excerpts from the book, had her own traffic story to share as she took to the stage. “I am sorry I’m late, but it’s not my fault. It’s that traffic; I think all of you must have faced it. I’m coming from Vasant Vihar and then for some reason I went to another hotel, I have no idea why,” she said, drawing attention to a predicament many in the gathering could relate to. The evening continued with readings from the book by authors William Dalrymple, Laila Tyabji and Sanjoy Roy.
Article Summary: The launch of Rakhshanda Jalil's book The Aunts of Gangapur turned into a grand gathering of friends and familiar faces from Delhi's literary and cultural circles. While the book remained the focus of the evening, Delhi’s traffic managed to become a talking point of its own.

Article Title: Infant among 3 killed as dumper truck rams auto-rickshaw in Delhi, leaves 5 injured
Article Text:
A devastating collision between a dumper truck and an auto-rickshaw took place in Sonia Vihar, Delhi (Representative image generated using AI)





NEW DELHI: Three people, including an infant girl, were killed and five others injured after a dumper truck collided with an auto-rickshaw near Pusta No. 5 in Delhi's Sonia Vihar on Thursday.A three-year-old girl escaped unhurt in the accident, while the injured were rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment.According to the initial report, eight people sustained injuries in the collision. The injured were taken to Jag Pravesh Hospital by members of the public and PCR personnel before the arrival of the Delhi Fire Service (DFS).Three victims, including two unidentified men and an infant girl, were declared brought dead at the hospital.The injured have been identified as Raja (32) and Rakhi (30), while the identities of two other men and a woman are yet to be ascertained.The Delhi Fire Service responded to the accident with two water tenders, one Quick Response Vehicle and an IRT team under the supervision of Station Officer Manoj Tyagi.At around 8.20am, Tyagi returned from the accident site and reported details of the incident.
Article Summary: A dumper truck collided with an auto-rickshaw near Pusta No. 5 in Delhi's Sonia Vihar. A three-year-old girl escaped unhurt in the accident, while the injured were rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment.

Article Title: Ibrahim Ali Khan turns heads in Bharat Reshma outift at Bombay Times Fashion Week
Article Text: The pearl-white Bhagalpuri silk indo that actor Ibrahim Ali Khan wore as the showstopper for Bharat Reshma at the Bombay Times Fashion Week recently became a talking point in fashion circles. Styled as a front-open jacket, with resham and light golden zardozi hand embroidery running across it in gold floral and paisley patterns, the outfit was finished with detailed borders.Statement shoulder jewellery on both sides gives the look its distinctive silhouette and regal couture feel. The outfit took 280 hours of handwork. “A little royal, a little rebellious,” said designers Bharat and Reshma Grover about the outfit, adding, “We wanted traditional royalty with a modern twist. Gold, grandeur and a unique style of jewellery.”Bharat Reshma, one of India’s top menswear designers, is the couture house founded by Bharat and Reshma Grover in 1991. Thirty-five years on, the label used the evening to unveil TVARA 2027, its latest collection. Built around the modern groom, the collection pairs traditional Indian craftsmanship with a contemporary eye for men who like to stand apart.The designers' line-up included sharply tailored tuxedos, intricately crafted designer sherwanis, unconventional kurta silhouettes and experimental designs. Every look was finished with fine detailing and a bespoke approach.For the designers, luxury is personal. They believe menswear should carry a man’s personality, confidence and individuality, and TVARA 2027 holds on to heritage while speaking to modern tastes. “We didn’t just showcase the outfits. We showcased the future,” said Bharat and Reshma Grover.The audience included Neil Nitin Mukesh, Maniesh Paul and director Siddharth P Malhotra, alongside a mix of celebrities, influencers and fashion industry names.
Article Summary: Bharat Reshma is one of India’s top menswear designers. The couture house was founded by Bharat and Reshma Grover in 1991. TVARA 2027 is built around the modern groom. The collection pairs traditional Indian craftsmanship with a contemporary eye for men who like to stand apart.

Article Title: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar markets buzz late into night on eve of Laxmi Pujan
Article Text:
From Paithan Gate to Tilak Path, Nirala Bazaar, Osmanpura, Gulmandi, City Chowk, Rangar Galli, Garkheda, Jalna Road, and CIDCO-HUDCO, shoppers thronged the streets with their families

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The city was soaked in Diwali colours on the eve of Laxmi Pujan, with markets buzzing late into the night.From Paithan Gate to Tilak Path, Nirala Bazaar, Osmanpura, Gulmandi, City Chowk, Rangar Galli, Garkheda, Jalna Road, and CIDCO-HUDCO, shoppers thronged the streets with their families. Readymade garment showrooms saw long waiting times, while stalls selling electric lights, decorative items, rangoli colours, puja materials, and festive food did brisk business.“Buying clothes for our two children proved to be a very tough task as every shop was heavily crowded. We did not expect such a huge rush and will ensure we shop well in advance next time,” said Sonali Upadhye, a homemaker.Old Mondha, Jadhavwadi, and local malls witnessed heavy grocery buying for Diwali snacks. Meanwhile, jewellery showrooms and automobile dealerships are gearing up for padwa, which is traditionally considered highly auspicious for buying gold and vehicles.The firecracker markets at Karnapura, Kalagram, TV Centre, Shivajinagar, Cantonment, Waluj, and the taluka town of Gangapur have also turned into major attractions, especially for youngsters eyeing new, viral fireworks.With schools already closed for the Diwali vacations, children were seen having a merry time.“We play a lot during Diwali vacations, burst firecrackers, and eat a lot of sweets. Diwali vacations end all too fast, though,” said Sarvesh Nanajkar, a primary school student.The Diwali festivities began on Thursday with Vasubaras, as families worshipped cows and calves by visiting nearby gaushalas and decorating their courtyards with rangolis. By Friday evening, the festive mood had completely shifted into full celebration mode.
Article Summary: The city was soaked in Diwali colours on the eve of Laxmi Pujan, with markets buzzing late into the night. Firecracker markets at Karnapura, Kalagram, TV Centre, Shivajinagar, Cantonment, Waluj, and the taluka town of Gangapur have also turned into major attractions.
